A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relative importance of the HNA cells was inversely related (although weak) to the bacterial pro- duction.
the %HNA and the mean side scatter (SSC, an indicator of cell size and density) of the HNA group are related to environmental parameters, but these relationships change with depth.
the %HNA was positively related to bacterial production in the surface layer (r 2 = 1.00) but negatively related to bacterial production at depth (r 2= 0.19, p<0.01).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relative importance of high nucleic-acid cells (as a percentage of the total) is inversely related to bacteri- al production, although this relationship is weak.
the relative abundance of HNA and the cytometric characteristics of HNA cells vary with depth, and that these variations are more pronounced than the variations with longitude.

the relative abundance and flow cytometric characteristics of HNA cells vary with depth and with longitude in the Mediterranean Sea and that vertical stratifica- tion plays an important role in the distribution of these cells.
